clue.text: Odd cat heard making disturbance

indicators.note: heard tells us the words for odd cat are only spoken, and the entry follows their sound

parts.note: odd means rum, and a cat is a puss

explanation.surface: Someone hears a strange cat yowling and blames it for a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy commotion or row, a synonym for a disturbance.

clue.text: Animal's call of rage

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, an animal
to page someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A beast lets out a furious bellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of violent, uncontrolled behaviour, a fit of rage.

clue.text: Gardening material — there's lots round Leatherhead

indicators.note: round places the word for lots around another letter

parts.note: much means a lot
read as leather head, the head or first letter of leather

explanation.surface: Gardeners in the Surrey town of Leatherhead have plenty of compost.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a town in Surrey, England, but here it splits as the head of 'leather', L.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulch is a layer of compost or bark spread over soil, a gardening material.

clue.text: Lingerie with flower on beneath

indicators.note: on says the river is added on after the other piece

parts.note: beneath means under
a flower is something that flows, a river: the Wear in north-east England

explanation.surface: Underclothes decorated with a flower worn underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river here, one that flows: the Wear runs through Durham.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear, so the general term covers it.

clue.text: Declined to be joined together again

definitions.meaning: to decline an offer is to turn it down, past tense
fused a second time, melted and joined anew

explanation.surface: Something refused to be glued back together.
explanation.definitionFit: Refused is the plain past tense of turning down; re-fused is the welding sense with the prefix re-.

clue.text: It goes round both ways

indicators.note: both ways says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something spins whichever way you look at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is anything that rotates or turns round.

clue.text: Dowdy woman with powerful hindquarters

parts.note: f stands for forte, strong or loud in music
the rump is the hindquarters

explanation.surface: An unfashionable woman with a large behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A frump is a woman who dresses in a dull, unfashionable way.

clue.text: Water supplier to support tube

parts.note: a stand is a support
a pipe is a tube

explanation.surface: A water company backs a pipeline.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpipe is a vertical pipe giving water in the street when mains supply is cut.

clue.text: Letter in boring yet showy style

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the adjective, in a showy style

indicators.note: in places the name of the letter inside the word for boring

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
ess is the spelt name of the letter S

explanation.surface: An essay written in a dull yet flamboyant manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy means stylish and elaborate, suited to showy occasions.

clue.text: So rams play in the marsh

indicators.note: play has the letters moving about freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Male sheep frolic in the bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a boggy area of land, a marsh.

clue.text: To some degree, the French Right appears inept

parts.note: MA, the Master of Arts, is some degree a graduate may hold
la is the French feminine word for the
droit is French for a right, also an English legal term for a right

explanation.surface: A French right-wing party is partly accused of incompetence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some degree' looks like a hedge meaning partly, but it gives MA, the Master of Arts degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit is a synonym for clumsy and unskilful, just as inept means lacking skill.

clue.text: This country's at sea over Russian edict

parts.note: for a British setter this country is the UK

indicators.note: over here means upset or knocked over, so the letters of sea are rearranged

explanation.surface: Britain is all at sea about some decree from Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the anagram signal, turning SEA into ASE; 'at' is a link, though 'at sea' looks like the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was a decree issued by the Tsar of Russia, so an edict from a Russian ruler.

clue.text: Hate to see sailor having initially nothing right

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: initially picks out only the opening letter of the word having

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone hates seeing a sailor who started out with no rights.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to loathe it, a stronger synonym for hate.

clue.text: Article has hint on poems from Australia

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tip is a hint
odes are poems

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece offers advice about poetry written down under.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antipodes is the British name for Australia and New Zealand, on the opposite side of the globe.

clue.text: Particularly intended for former journalists

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Something is meant specifically for retired reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Express is also a British newspaper, which suits the journalists of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Express as an adjective means specific or deliberate, as in an express purpose.

clue.text: Outlaw professional writer

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A professional author is banned.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe is to forbid or outlaw.

clue.text: Garrison's inner retreat with revolutionary turn to it

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
a U-turn is a turn, so U
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers fall back into the inner keep while a rebel wheels round to face it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduit is a keep or inner stronghold of a fort, where a garrison can retreat.

clue.text: Say bad things of French granite pieces

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: pieces suggests broken bits, so the letters of granite are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone badmouths broken lumps of French stone.
explanation.definitionFit: To denigrate is to belittle or criticise unfairly.

clue.text: He wrote a dance in a car once

definitions.meaning: William ..., the Victorian writer and designer
an English folk dance with bells and sticks
A British car make, now defunct

explanation.surface: A writer is said to have danced in an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one name: the writer William Morris, morris dancing, and the old Morris motor car.

clue.text: It's worn by a tyrannical employer

definitions.meaning: a knitted pullover, a garment
one who sweats workers, making them toil for low pay

explanation.surface: A pullover is worn by a harsh boss.
explanation.walkthrough: A sweater, in the old sense, is a boss who runs a sweatshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweater is both the jumper and an exploiter who sweats labour.

clue.text: Satisfied with what's inside

definitions.meaning: pleased and at ease, the adjective stressed on the second syllable
the ... held in a container, the noun stressed on the first syllable

explanation.surface: Someone is happy with the contents of the box.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling serves as an adjective meaning pleased and a noun meaning the matter contained.

clue.text: Wine-coloured bird

definitions.meaning: a sweet wine from the ... Islands
the bright yellow colour
a yellow songbird

explanation.surface: A bird with plumage the colour of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Canary is a sweet island wine, a bright yellow and the singing finch.

clue.text: Book man going to grass

definitions.meaning: a book of the New Testament
a man's name
a meadow grass grown for hay

explanation.surface: A man in a book goes to seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is a New Testament book, a male name and a hay grass.

clue.text: Dog was first and played on ice

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: A dog went ahead and skated about.
explanation.definitionFit: Curled is the past tense of curl, to play curling, sliding stones on ice.

clue.text: Lack of interest in United Nations business?

parts.note: a concern is a business or firm

explanation.surface: Apathy is found in the affairs of the UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcern is indifference, an absence of care or interest.

clue.text: Drink with Emperor of Ethiopia

definitions.meaning: a hot drink of wine, water, sugar and spice
the title of the Ethiopian ruler

explanation.surface: The Ethiopian emperor takes a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is a mulled wine drink and the Amharic title for an emperor.

clue.text: Tidy gravity chamber

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity
a room is a chamber

explanation.surface: A neat, serious-looking room.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to make neat and tidy, as with hair or a horse.

clue.text: Hold forth of the cost of a ring?

parts.note: a ring is round, the letter O
a rate is a cost or charge

explanation.surface: Someone holds forth about the price of a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The rate of an O, the cost of a ring, reads backwards into the answer's order.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak at length in a pompous way, to hold forth.

clue.text: Self-divided psychiatrist ladling out 550

indicators.note: out says that letters are taken away from the word ladling

parts.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and L is 50

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist with a split personality serves soup from a big pot.
explanation.walkthrough: R. D. Laing, the Scottish psychiatrist, wrote The Divided Self, hence 'Self-divided'.
explanation.definitionFit: R. D. Laing was the psychiatrist who wrote The Divided Self, a study of schizophrenia.

clue.text: Jolly Turkish officer intent on exposing virago

annotationWithheld.why: Jolly Turkish officer intent on exposing virago (9): RM + AGA inside TENT needs 'intent' read as 'in tent', so the one word is both the container indicator and the TENT fodder
annotationWithheld.clue: Jolly Turkish officer intent on exposing virago

clue.text: Item of furniture found in the theatre?

definitions.meaning: a sideboard with shelves for plates
a person who helps actors into costume backstage

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture turns up at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is both a kitchen sideboard and a theatre assistant who looks after costumes.

clue.text: Cure variation in weight of coins

definitions.meaning: a treatment that heals
the mint term for the tolerance allowed in a coin's weight or fineness

explanation.surface: A treatment for coins of uneven weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedy means a cure, and in minting is the permitted deviation from standard coin weight.
